---
title: "Interval Loading"
format: html
---

## Overview

Digital interval series stores start/end periods (for example stimulus windows, trial epochs, contact bouts).

Supported interval formats:

| Format | Typical Source | Available In |
|---|---|---|
| `csv` (start/end pairs) | Interval tables with two columns | Data Import Widget and JSON |
| `csv` with `csv_layout: "binary_state"` | Time + binary state columns (0/1) | JSON workflows |
| `binary` / `uint16` | TTL extraction from packed digital words | Data Import Widget (build-dependent) and JSON |

::: {.callout-note}
## JSON Data Type Name
Use `"data_type": "digital_interval"` in JSON.
:::

## Data Import Widget

Open **Modules -> Data Import**, choose **Digital Interval Series**.

### CSV mode

- file path
- delimiter
- header toggle
- start column
- end column

### Binary mode

If enabled in your build, widget options include:

- `header_size_bytes`
- `data_type_bytes` (1/2/4/8)
- `channel`
- `transition_type` (`rising` or `falling`)

## JSON: CSV Start/End Intervals (`format: "csv"`)

```json
{
  "filepath": "behavior/trials.csv",
  "data_type": "digital_interval",
  "name": "trial_epochs",
  "format": "csv",
  "delimiter": ",",
  "has_header": true,
  "start_column": 0,
  "end_column": 1,
  "clock": "master"
}
```

| Element | Required? | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `delimiter` | No | string | `","` | Column delimiter |
| `has_header` | No | boolean | `false` | Skip first row when true |
| `start_column` | No | integer | `0` | 0-based start-time column |
| `end_column` | No | integer | `1` | 0-based end-time column |
| `clock` | No | string | `"time"` | Assigns this data to an existing TimeFrame |

## JSON: CSV Binary-State Layout (`format: "csv"`, `csv_layout: "binary_state"`)

Use this when each row is a time sample and each data column is a 0/1 trace.

### Load one binary-state column

```json
{
  "filepath": "daq/events_table.dat",
  "data_type": "digital_interval",
  "name": "laser",
  "format": "csv",
  "csv_layout": "binary_state",
  "header_lines_to_skip": 5,
  "time_column": 0,
  "data_column": 3,
  "delimiter": "\t",
  "binary_threshold": 0.5,
  "sampling_rate": 14000.0
}
```

### Load all binary-state columns

```json
{
  "filepath": "daq/events_table.dat",
  "data_type": "digital_interval",
  "name": "channels",
  "format": "csv",
  "csv_layout": "binary_state",
  "all_columns": true,
  "header_lines_to_skip": 5,
  "time_column": 0,
  "delimiter": "\t",
  "binary_threshold": 0.5,
  "sampling_rate": 14000.0
}
```

| Element | Required? | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `csv_layout` | Yes (for this mode) | string | `"intervals"` | Must be `"binary_state"` |
| `header_lines_to_skip` | No | integer | `5` | Lines skipped before the header row |
| `time_column` | No | integer | `0` | 0-based time column |
| `data_column` | No | integer | `1` | 0-based binary-state column |
| `delimiter` | No | string | tab (`"\t"`) | Column delimiter |
| `binary_threshold` | No | number | `0.5` | Values >= threshold are treated as ON |
| `sampling_rate` | No | number | `0.0` | Multiplier for fractional time to integer indices |
| `all_columns` | No | boolean | `false` | If true, create one series per data column |

::: {.callout-tip}
With `all_columns: true`, each non-time column is loaded as a separate interval series, and output names are derived from the column headers.
:::

## JSON: Binary TTL Intervals (`format: "binary"` or `"uint16"`)

```json
{
  "filepath": "daq/ttl.bin",
  "data_type": "digital_interval",
  "name": "laser_window",
  "format": "binary",
  "channel": 2,
  "transition": "rising",
  "header_size": 0,
  "channel_count": 1
}
```

| Element | Required? | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `channel` | Yes | integer | - | Bit index to extract |
| `transition` | Yes | string | - | `"rising"` or `"falling"` interval polarity |
| `header_size` | No | integer | `0` | Bytes to skip at file start |
| `channel_count` | No | integer | `1` | Interleaved channel count |
